topic: Smoking cessation in mental health inpatients

audits.title: Audit of inpatient smoking cessation advice
audits.standard: Smoking status asked on admission and cessation advice or nicotine replacement therapy offered (target not reported)
audits.setting: Four general adult acute psychiatric wards, Aneurin Bevan Health Board

cycle1.result: Smoking status asked in 68%; not asked n = 11 (32%); smoker not given advice n = 13 (38%); smoker given advice n = 4 (12%); advice or NRT given to only 14% of potential smokers.

audits.other_findings: Asking about smoking varied between wards and there was a lack of smoking cessation literature on the wards.
audits.citation: Mohamed F, Bader M. Audit of inpatient smoking cessation advice. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S92-S93. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.280.

audits.title: A quality improvement project on nicotine replacement therapy in Shannon Clinic (Northern Ireland)
audits.standard: Correct prescribing of nicotine replacement therapy on drug charts
audits.setting: Shannon Clinic (smoke-free inpatient unit), Northern Ireland

cycle1.result: 22% of drug charts had nicotine replacement therapy prescribed incorrectly.

audits.intervention: Poster showing how to prescribe nicotine replacement therapy correctly placed on each ward.

cycle2.result: 0% of drug charts had nicotine replacement therapy prescribed incorrectly.

audits.other_findings: There was no clear local guidance on NRT prescribing before the project.
audits.citation: Moss E. A quality improvement project on nicotine replacement therapy in Shannon Clinic (Northern Ireland). BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S211-S211. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.564.

audits.title: Improving Clinical Care in Tobacco and Smoking-Related Problems: A Report of Clinical Audit and Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: NICE guideline 'Smoking: acute, maternity and mental health services'
audits.setting: General adult inpatient mental health units, Wrexham, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board

cycle1.result: 71.88% asked about smoking history; under 10% assessed in detail.

audits.intervention: PowerPoint presentation shared on measurement tools for assessing smoking behaviour (after a first re-audit with no intervention).

cycle2.result: 57.14% assessed for smoking; under 40% assessed in detail.

audits.other_findings: The first re-audit without intervention (19 admissions) fell to 36.84%, under 16% in detail. Doctor rotation may explain the small change; teaching at the start of each rotation is planned.
audits.citation: Loo J, Raja J, Anyanwu U, Shankar N, Elsayed A, Azahr Z, et al.. Improving Clinical Care in Tobacco and Smoking-Related Problems: A Report of Clinical Audit and Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S148-S149. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.424.

audits.title: An Audit to Assess Nicotine Management on a Mental Health Rehabilitation Unit in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.setting: Rathbone Rehabilitation Centre, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Smoking status recorded 47 (92%); 26/28 (93%) smokers offered support on admission; 24/31 (77%) offered support at regular intervals; 20/28 (71%) offered NRT; 5/31 referred to Nicotine Dependence Treatment Advisor.

audits.intervention: Action plan: reminders via team meetings and emails, completion of physical health nursing proforma, and posters on the referral pathway
audits.citation: Baruah R, Popoola O, Gilbey S, Pentz O. An Audit to Assess Nicotine Management on a Mental Health Rehabilitation Unit in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S219-S219. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.541.

audits.title: Audit of Nicotine Replacement Therapy Practices and Vaping Use in Inpatients: Adherence to Dual NRT Regimen and Documentation of Smoking Cessation Plans
audits.standard: EPUT nicotine prescribing guidelines and British Thoracic Society recommended dual NRT regimen; documentation of smoking status and cessation plans
audits.setting: Four Mid-Essex general adult inpatient wards, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 57% were smokers and 72% of smokers used vapes. None were on dual NRT; no cessation plans for anyone using NRT. 75% had a documented discussion about smoking and nicotine use, not all including NRT options.

audits.intervention: None reported; recommendations include asking all patients about smoking status, early dual NRT, documenting vaping, cessation plans in physical health checks and a dual NRT prescribing bundle. Follow-up audit in 4-5 months recommended.
audits.other_findings: Most patients relied solely on short-acting NRT such as vapes and inhalators; vaping was poorly documented.
audits.citation: Bergman M, Sule A. Audit of Nicotine Replacement Therapy Practices and Vaping Use in Inpatients: Adherence to Dual NRT Regimen and Documentation of Smoking Cessation Plans. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S221-S221. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10557.

audits.title: Enhancing Smoking Cessation Support: Audit of Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT) in Psychiatric Inpatient Care
audits.standard: Smoking status documented; NRT within four hours of admission; contraindications documented; drug interactions considered
audits.setting: Adult psychiatry inpatient wards, North Wales

cycle1.result: Smoking status assessed 79%; NRT within four hours 59%; contraindications and drug interactions considered 14%.

audits.other_findings: Recommendations: clinician training and a standardised NRT tool.

audits.title: Adherence to Smoking Cessation Policy in Inpatient Psychiatric Services at Hamad Hospital: A Retrospective Clinical Audit
audits.standard: Institutional Smoking Cessation Policy (smoking status, dependence severity, NRT initiation and monitoring, education, referral, discharge planning)
audits.setting: Inpatient psychiatric units, Hamad Hospital (Hamad Medical Corporation)

cycle1.result: Initial nicotine dependence screening >97%; dependence severity documented in 30.2%; appropriate NRT strength 12.3%; NRT side-effect monitoring 0%; 20% of smokers received NRT; Tobacco Control Center referral 18%; motivational interventions 1.8%; patient/family education 0%; NRT on discharge summary 3.3%.

audits.intervention: Recommended targeted staff training, better access to educational resources and structured monitoring and documentation systems.
audits.other_findings: About 40% of admitted patients were current smokers; 29% declined NRT.
audits.citation: Hamad S, Alater A, Iqbal Y, Sinha P, Ali M. Adherence to Smoking Cessation Policy in Inpatient Psychiatric Services at Hamad Hospital: A Retrospective Clinical Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S276-S276. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11562.

audits.title: Baseline Audit of Smoke-Free Policy Compliance on Older Adult Psychiatric Inpatient Wards
audits.standard: Trust Smoke-Free standards: smoking status documented on admission; tobacco dependence treatment within 30 minutes; regular MDT review; referral to Tobacco Dependency Team within 24 hours
audits.setting: Four older adult psychiatric inpatient wards (Lancashire and South Cumbria Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: Smoking status documented 31% (16/53); treatment within 30 minutes 0%; 83% of smokers eventually prescribed NRT, all >5 hours after admission; MDT review 0%; referral within 24 hours 17%.

audits.other_findings: Only 6 patients had documented tobacco dependence. Re-audit planned after interventions.
audits.citation: Revitt L, Egbegbedia A. Baseline Audit of Smoke-Free Policy Compliance on Older Adult Psychiatric Inpatient Wards. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S288-S289. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11730.

audits.title: Audit of Smoking Status Documentation and Smoking Cessation Interventions in Psychiatric Inpatients Department of Psychiatry, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore
audits.setting: Department of Psychiatry, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore

cycle1.period: Two cycles over 2 months (dates not stated)
cycle1.result: Smoking status documented in 66.7%; among 12 smokers: brief advice 33.3%, NRT offered 25%, referral 8.3%, follow-up plan 16.7%.

audits.intervention: Staff education, reminders during admission clerking and emphasis on documenting smoking cessation measures.

cycle2.result: Smoking status documented in 93.3%; among 13 smokers: brief advice 84.6%, NRT 76.9%, referral 53.8%, follow-up plan 69.2%.

audits.other_findings: Regular re-audit recommended to sustain compliance.
audits.citation: Ali M, Siraj S, Ijaz M, Zahid A, Arshad M. Audit of Smoking Status Documentation and Smoking Cessation Interventions in Psychiatric Inpatients Department of Psychiatry, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S345-S345. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11841.

audits.title: Re-Audit of Documentation of Smoking and E-Cigarette Use History in Inpatient Medical Records on a Medium Secure Rehabilitation Ward
audits.setting: 16-bed male medium secure rehabilitation ward, Cumbria Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: E-cigarette and smoking history was not recorded.

audits.intervention: Standardised smoking/vaping history and dependence checklists adapted for the setting and used for new admissions; existing patients interviewed retrospectively.

cycle2.result: Both new admissions had a thorough smoking and vaping history documented.

audits.other_findings: Of 13 patients assessed, all had smoked, 10/13 had used e-cigarettes (mostly starting in hospital or prison) and eight had high e-cigarette dependence; most had no health concerns about vaping.
audits.citation: Robinson P, Maryam H, Shehab A, Sud N. Re-Audit of Documentation of Smoking and E-Cigarette Use History in Inpatient Medical Records on a Medium Secure Rehabilitation Ward. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S349-S350. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11850.

audits.title: An audit on smoking status identification and cessation support in a psychiatric inpatient setting
audits.standard: Documentation of smoking status, cessation advice or referral, and medication adjustment for smoking status change
audits.setting: Mount Carmel Hospital, psychiatric inpatient admissions

cycle1.result: Smoking status documented in 87.7%; 113 (51.6%) current smokers; only one discharge letter mentioned cessation advice or referral; no documented medication adjustments for smoking status.

audits.other_findings: Smoking was associated with male sex, younger age, secondary education and alcohol use disorders (89% smokers, OR 15).
audits.citation: Montebello G, Grech G, Bonello D, Galea M, Callus K, Purkiss C. An audit on smoking status identification and cessation support in a psychiatric inpatient setting. European Psychiatry. 2026;69(S1):S451-S452. doi:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2026.10844.
